1635.text: **LEVEL DRIFT IS SUFFICIENT TO SUPPLY ROUGHLY HALF THE MERGE'S SPATIAL SWING, AND THAT IS A LOWER BOUND.** Over the same six windows, drift peak-to-peak against the merge's spatial sd expressed as a fraction of level: median **52% of the gate-0 swing and 56% of the gate-4 swing**, ranging 26%-175% window to window. **The figure is a lower bound on drift's share of the ARTIFACT**, because the denominator is the window's total spatial variation and some of those windows contain genuine scene structure (two swing 13-18%, far above any plausible artifact). **Sufficiency is not attribution** -- nothing here shows that removing the drift removes the artifact, only that the drift is large enough to account for a large share of it. |

1636.label: ARGUED
1636.text: **CONFIRMED in part by facts 1637-1638 (visible fix on one of three subjects; the promotion question is now 203).** **ON THIS EVIDENCE `STREHL_PHOTOMETRIC` IS THE BEST-EVIDENCED UNTESTED IMPROVEMENT AVAILABLE TO THE SHIPPED RENDER, AND NOBODY HAS RUN IT.** The chain: the merge gathers different frames in different regions; those frames differ by several percent in level (fact 1633, M24); the difference is a smooth ramp a gain fit removes (fact 1634); and it is large enough to supply about half the observed swing (fact 1635). The correction exists and is **default OFF** (`main.rs:284`). **This is a prediction, not a result** -- it was pre-registered to M116 with the instrument to test it (`patchwork_invariant.py`, baseline 1.114x and 7/12 at the shipped gate) and the instruction not to evaluate it on `109MSDCF`, which M24 measured at 0.91% and is the quietest stack in the corpus. **A null would be valuable**: it would rule out level drift and point at the focus decision itself. |

1637.label: MEASURED
1637.text: **`--photometric` REMOVES FINE STRUCTURE FROM SMOOTH BACKGROUND ON ONE OF THREE SUBJECTS AND IS INERT ON THE OTHER TWO.** Scored M116's own A0 (default) and A1 (`--photometric`) arms -- same frozen warp map, so registration is held constant -- on 12 windows per subject chosen from the **symmetric mean of the two arms**, so neither arm picks the pixels it is judged on (`experiments/ORCH-drift-check/photometric_ab.py`). Laplacian-RMS ratio, test over base: **`tweezers-cpl` median 0.710**, and within it the effect tracks window smoothness -- the six smoothest windows fall **0.632 to 0.812** while textured windows sit at **0.99 to 1.03**. `bee-3-cpl` median **1.064** and `foam` **1.013**, both roughly uniform across smooth and textured windows. In the subject that moves, the test arm converges to a **floor near 45-53 counts** from a base of 56-79. |

1638.label: MEASURED
1638.text: **AND THE PIXELS SHOW WHAT THE NUMBER MEANS: THE DEFAULT MERGE COVERS A DEFOCUSED BACKGROUND IN BLOTCHES AND `--photometric` REMOVES THEM.** At `tweezers-cpl` x=912 y=400 under a **shared stretch taken from the base arm** (`PHOTOMETRIC-tweezers-cpl-smooth-912x400.png`), the default arm shows dozens of soft oval patches over a smooth tonal gradient; the photometric arm shows the gradient and no patches. **A defocused region cannot contain structure at that scale** -- defocus is a low-pass filter -- so the patches are manufactured, which is the invariant of fact 1631 stated visually. **The blur control passes:** at x=400 y=656 the tweezer edge, its grain and the speckled texture are preserved indistinguishably, so this is not smoothing. Cost is **+3.7 s mean over three subjects (45.81 -> 49.52 s)** and on `tweezers-cpl` the photometric arm was **faster** (52.01 -> 45.80 s), so run-to-run variance exceeds the effect. **This is the first measured, visible removal of the mosaic from a shipped-path render.** |

1639.label: MEASURED
1639.text: **M116'S `KEEP-OFF` VERDICT ON PHOTOMETRIC IS NOT REFUTED BY THIS -- ITS BAR WAS ON THE WRONG AXIS.** M116 scored the identical arms with a global sharpness statistic and measured **+0.00477 (bee), -0.00003 (foam), +0.00835 (tweezers) against a +0.010 promotion bar**, and returned KEEP-OFF. **Every one of those numbers is at or above zero** -- its own data says the instrument never hurt sharpness on any subject -- and the arm simply failed a threshold defined on an axis the defect does not live on. The defect is **tonal**: patchy per-region level offsets change tone, not sharpness. Both measurements are correct and they are measuring different things. |

1640.label: ARGUED
1640.text: **THE MECHANISM CHAIN FOR THE MOSAIC IS NOW COMPLETE END TO END, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS MORE THAN ONE SUBJECT'S RESULT.** Frames differ in level by 3.2-8.4% peak-to-peak (fact 1633, corroborating M24); the difference is a smooth ramp in frame index that a per-frame gain fit removes almost entirely (fact 1634, 91.8% of variance); the merge elects different frames in different regions; so regions inherit different levels and the background acquires plateaus (fact 1638's blotches); and fitting the gain removes them (facts 1637, 1638). **Every link is measured.** The prediction that survives is that a subject shows the defect in proportion to its level drift, which explains why `bee-3-cpl` -- whose default background already sits at 33-47 counts, **smoother than the photometric arm on `tweezers-cpl`** -- has nothing to fix. **Untested:** whether that proportionality holds across the corpus. That is the measurement that would justify flipping the default, and it needs the drift figure and the blotch figure on the same stacks. |

1641.label: MEASURED
1641.text: **THE SOFT GATE BEATS `--photometric` ON THE TONAL STATISTIC AND IS DISQUALIFIED BY THE BLUR CONTROL.** Scoring M116's remaining arms with the fact-1637 instrument -- laplacian-RMS ratio against the default, identical windows across arms -- the soft-gate arms have the **better headline number on every subject**: `tweezers-cpl` **0.553** (gaussian), **0.562** (exponential), **0.544** (gaussian + photometric) against **0.710** for photometric alone, and `bee-3-cpl` **0.808 / 0.819 / 0.809** against **1.064**. **But on `bee-3-cpl` the gaussian soft gate cuts the TEXTURED control window by 30.5% (500.8 -> 348.0), which is as large as its effect on that subject's smooth windows (0.851 / 0.673 / 0.813).** Photometric's textured windows are **1.037** (bee) and **1.027** (tweezers) -- preserved. Confirmed by eye on a shared stretch: the soft-gate panel smears the fine hairs along the leg edge and erases a highlight that the default resolves. |

1642.label: MEASURED
1642.text: **WHICH MEANS THE TWO INSTRUMENTS NOW AGREE ON THE SOFT GATE AND DISAGREE ONLY ON PHOTOMETRIC -- AND THE BLUR CONTROL IS WHAT SEPARATES THE TWO CASES.** M116 rejected the soft gate on a detail statistic at **-0.01218**, and fact 1641 rejects it on a background statistic plus a control, by a different route, on different windows, with a different measure. **Two independent methods converging on the same verdict is much stronger than either alone.** The photometric disagreement (fact 1639) survives this because it is the one arm whose control window is untouched: it is the only candidate that changes smooth regions **without** changing textured ones. `A4` (photometric + gaussian soft gate) inherits the blur -- bee textured **0.711** -- so the combination is not a way to keep both. |

1643.label: MEASURED
1643.text: **AND THE RANKING WOULD HAVE BEEN WRONG WITHOUT THE CONTROL.** On the defect statistic alone the correct promotion order is soft-gate-gaussian > soft-gate-exponential > photometric on both subjects that move. After the blur control it is photometric alone, and the top two are defects. **The statistic that identified the defect could not, by itself, tell a fix from a blur** -- removing structure scores identically either way, and only the region where structure is legitimate distinguishes them. |

1644.label: MEASURED
1644.text: **THE BLUR CONTROL IS NOW STRUCTURAL, AND IT REPRODUCES THE HAND VERDICT ON ITS OWN.** `experiments/ORCH-drift-check/switch_gate.py` scores a candidate on two axes in one pass -- **removal** on the 8 smoothest windows and **preservation** on the 8 most textured -- both pools drawn from the symmetric mean of the two arms, and returns PASS only when `removal <= 0.97` **and** `preservation >= 0.97`, so the control holds a veto rather than a footnote. On M116's arms it recovers facts 1641-1643 with no human in the loop: `A1` (`--photometric`) shows **no harm on any subject** -- bee `1.0583 / 1.0324`, foam `1.0111 / 1.0080`, tweezers `0.8264 / 1.0208` PASS -- while `A2`, `A3` and `A4` are all REJECTED on `bee-3-cpl` at preservation **0.6703 / 0.6345 / 0.6839**. |

1645.label: MEASURED
1645.text: **AND THE HARM IS VISIBLE ON EXACTLY ONE OF THE THREE SUBJECTS.** On `tweezers-cpl` alone every soft-gate variant **passes its own texture control** -- preservation **0.9918 / 0.9911 / 1.0141** -- while posting the **best removal scores in the entire candidate set**, **0.5493 / 0.5622 / 0.5299** against `0.8264` for photometric. On `foam` every arm reads ~`0.99`-`1.01` on both axes, i.e. nothing. **Only `bee-3-cpl` exposes the blur at all.** So a campaign run on tweezers -- the subject that carries the photometric win, and therefore the natural one to test on -- would have ranked the soft gate first, cleared it on its control, and promoted a blur. Taking a median across the three subjects does the same thing, because two of them are silent. |

1646.label: MEASURED
1646.text: **THE INSTRUMENT IS COMMISSIONED BY REJECTING A BLUR, NOT BY DETECTING AN EFFECT.** `switch_gate.py` refuses to print a verdict on a subject until it has scored `PLANT-BLUR` -- the base arm passed through an `r=2` box blur and fed in as though it were a candidate -- and rejected it. It reads removal **0.1130 / 0.2873 / 0.1831** and preservation **0.1908 / 0.2678 / 0.2319** on bee / foam / tweezers and is REJECTED on all three. The null (`A0` against itself) reads exactly **1.0000** on both axes on all three subjects, and the voronoi plant clears its `>1.30` / `<0.77` bars on all three. **A plant that shows an instrument is sensitive says nothing about whether it is specific**; this is the control for specificity and it is the one the earlier instrument lacked. |

1647.label: MEASURED
1647.text: **M111 IS NOT EXPOSED TO THE PIL HAZARD, AND IT RE-RAN RATHER THAN ARGUED.** Across all 33 files in the lane there are **zero `Image.open(` call sites**; every TIFF read is `tifffile.imread`, and the three scripts that import PIL use it only on the write path for PNG contact sheets. Rather than rest on that, M111 recomputed its headline `blobB` statistic through **both** readers with every other line identical. The reported values reproduce exactly through `tifffile` (interior ratio **0.094** merged / **0.761** control; boundary p90 **1384.04** / **226.69**), and the level loss on those very files is real -- **62152 -> 256** distinct levels on the merged render (**243x**), 49028 -> 245 on the control. Had PIL been used, `blobB` boundary hardness would have read **5.573x** instead of **6.105x** (**-8.7%**) and `blobA` **2.875x** instead of **3.111x** (-7.6%): **the defect would still have been detected, but understated**. |

1648.label: MEASURED
1648.text: **AND THE PIL DISTORTION IS DIRECTIONAL -- IT BIASES TOWARD THE NULL.** Within the same statistic the *small* term moves about **13x more** than the large one: the control's soft boundary p90 shifts **+10.5%** where the merged render's hard boundary shifts **+0.8%**. The mechanism is that quantisation error is an **absolute** floor, so it is a large fraction of a small quantity and a negligible fraction of a large one. **Consequence: every large-over-small ratio compresses toward 1.** That is precisely the direction that manufactures a **false clean null**, which is the hardest error in this project to catch, because nobody re-examines an arm that came back showing no effect. The broadcast hazard's 'most suspect of all' category now has a measured sign and magnitude. |

1649.label: MEASURED
1649.text: **EXPOSURE DEPENDS ON THE SHAPE OF THE STATISTIC, NOT ONLY ON THE DTYPE OF THE FILE.** In one script, on the **same pixels of the same file**, M111's interior-flatness ratio was nearly immune (**-0.0%**, **+3.0%**) while its boundary-hardness contrast lost **8.7%**. A ratio of two comparably-sized quantities largely survives; a contrast between a strong and a weak signal does not. This splits the hazard's 'suspect' bucket along a line that is not visible from the input file at all -- `gradient/high-frequency energy` and `retention ratios` land on **opposite sides** of it depending only on how they are formed. |

1650.label: MEASURED
1650.text: **THE MULTI-FRAME WIENER DECONVOLUTION MERGE HAS NO HEADROOM OVER THE MERGE THAT ALREADY SHIPS. DO NOT BUILD IT.** At matched contrast, focus-axis Wiener deconvolution beats the already-shipping noise-gated average by `R_SNR = **1.0014** +/- 0.0184`, 95% CI **[0.965, 1.038]** -- an interval that contains 1 and excludes any worthwhile gain. The diffraction-free matched filter reads **0.9844** +/- 0.0182, i.e. slightly *worse*. It **looks** dramatically better -- contrast reaches **2.51x** +/- 0.63 that of the sharpest frame at f=0.205 -- but noise rises to **2.03x** +/- 0.57 in step. **It reallocates information; it does not create it.** This refutes proposal 3 of the external review (`docs/proposals/2026-08-external-review.md`), which argued deconvolution was the only path to real sharpness at this rig's magnification. |

1651.label: MEASURED
1651.text: **AND IT RINGS.** The Wiener arms put **29.5-36.4%** of pixels outside the convex hull of the source stack -- values no input frame contains -- with a **halo peaking at 70.7%** of pixels in the 8-16 px shell around edges and a p99.9 excess of **18-26x** the hull width. **All five convex arms read exactly 0.0000%.** So the failure is not a tuning artefact of one parameter choice: it is the signature of the estimator class, and it is the same artefact family as the halo that is already this project's lead defect. |

1652.label: REFUTED
1652.text: **OTF SELF-CALIBRATION FROM THE THROUGH-FOCUS CURVE DOES NOT WORK.** The external review proposed that per-frame OTF widths could be self-calibrated from the through-focus response curve itself, so that no lens model would be load-bearing. Measured, the curve width **over-estimates `s` by 1.87x and 2.15x**, and the resulting model claims an **OTF magnitude of 0.021** at a frequency where direct measurement reads **0.638** -- wrong by a factor of 30. The guard that was supposed to make the deconvolution safe without a lens database is itself unsound. |

1653.label: MEASURED
1653.text: **M115'S PRE-REGISTERED PRIMARY CHANNEL FAILED ITS OWN NULL, AND FAILED IN THE DIRECTION OF ITS HYPOTHESIS.** The antithetic-injection channel returned **SNR 84.9 on a scene-free capture**, under-estimating noise **73x**, because the election flips on **100.0%** of tiles. M115 caught it, discarded the channel, and replaced it with a split-stack channel that carries no noise model and reads consistency **1.0000**. **Had the failed channel been trusted, every number in the report would have favoured deconvolution by an order of magnitude** -- i.e. the instrument's failure mode pointed precisely at the conclusion the milestone was dispatched hoping to find. |

1654.label: MEASURED
1654.text: **A SHARPNESS CLAIM REPORTED AS CONTRAST IS UNFALSIFIABLE; REPORTED AS SNR AT MATCHED CONTRAST IT IS NOT.** M115's gain-invariance control (C3) applied post-filters that changed measured contrast by up to **3.94x**: `R_SNR` moved **<= 0.54%**, while a naive gradient sharpness metric on the same arms was fooled by **8.25x**. The positive control (C2, exact Fourier blur) was monotone with 8/8 recovery ratios in **[0.9938, 0.9974]**. |

1655.label: MEASURED
1655.text: **THE PIL NARROWING IS WORSE THAN 241x ON LOW-CONTRAST CROPS, AND RATIO-OF-ARMS STATISTICS LARGELY SURVIVE IT.** M115 is not exposed (its only reader is `rawpy.imread`; inputs verified `uint16` at 2420 / 4906 / 7367 distinct levels), but it commissioned the check by planting the narrowing into its own loader. Three refinements to the hazard: (a) **damage scales with the file's OCCUPIED range, not the full 16-bit range** -- a detail ROI spanning ~2100 DN was left with **9 distinct levels, not 256**; (b) absolute readings are destroyed -- noise power **3.5x** too high, sigma off **1.9x**, band SNR **0.438x** of truth, and the OTF fit moved **+23.7%**; (c) **a ratio of two arms on the same data is largely protected by cancellation** -- `R_SNR(WIENER)/R_SNR(GATE)` moved only **-1.0%** (0.9340 -> 0.9248). |

1656.label: MEASURED
1656.text: **THE SPECTRAL ATTRIBUTION OF THE CA SCENE-DEPENDENCE IS NOT SUPPORTED, AND ITS ONE FALSIFIABLE PREDICTION CAME OUT BACKWARDS.** The hypothesis required that scenes weighted toward longer wavelengths in red need a *larger* red correction, monotonically. Pre-registered bar S6 required **positive** rho; across n=8 of the owner's stacks the measured Spearman rho is **-0.6905**, p=0.058 -- the wrong sign. It is not noise-limited: R/G spans **10.7%** while `needed` spans **27.3%**. M113 registered the bar as weak in advance and therefore reports NOT SUPPORTED rather than REFUTED, honouring its own pre-registration. |

1657.label: MEASURED
1657.text: **BUT THE SCENE-DEPENDENCE ITSELF IS CONFIRMED AND LARGER THAN FIRST THOUGHT.** `needed` runs **529.9 -> 674.7 ppm**, a spread of **27.3%** across eight stacks, against a measured replicate floor of **19.5 ppm** -- an effect roughly fourteen times the repeatability. All eight passed the fact-1569 chain-transfer instrument check at **0.9064-1.0004**. **So the correction genuinely differs between subjects and the mechanism is unidentified**; `scene-dependent` is established, `spectral` is not. |

1658.label: REFUTED
1658.text: **FOUR RIVAL EXPLANATIONS DIED ON EXISTING DATA, AND TWO OF THEM DIED ON EXIF ALONE.** Aperture and the teleconverter: **every `-cpl` stack in the corpus is f/5.6 on `FE 100mm F2.8 GM + 2X TC`**, so **there is no aperture contrast anywhere in the library** and an aperture ladder would vary a held-fixed variable. Magnification and focus distance: `bee-1-cpl` reads 536.2 ppm, **3.5 ppm** from the bee mean but **118.7 ppm** from `couch` at an identical focus distance. Subject radial structure: refuted to **+/-15 ppm**. A common scale error: refuted, CV of B/R **14.9%** against 24.7%. |

1659.label: MEASURED
1659.text: **THE ALIGNMENT RIVAL WAS REFUTED ONLY AFTER M113 CORRECTED ITS OWN FIRST ANSWER, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE TRANSFERABLE PART.** Its S5 test initially read a **64% pipeline contribution**, which would have moved most of the effect out of optics. **That was the test failing, not the pipeline:** defocused windows dilute the global fit. Re-run on `flat-on-ruler-cpl` -- flat, so the confound is **absent by construction** rather than corrected for -- the merge and a single un-aligned frame agree to **4.8 ppm**. Restricting the bee frame to its sharp quartile moves the reading **192.0 -> 623.5 ppm**, confirming the dilution mechanism directly. |

1660.label: MEASURED
1660.text: **`STREHL_FIX_CA` IS A SILENT NO-OP WHEN `STREHL_ALIGN=0`.** The arms come out **byte-identical with no warning of any kind**. Anyone A/B-ing the CA correction with registration disabled -- which is the natural way to isolate an optical correction from a geometric one -- would measure exactly nothing and correctly conclude the flag does nothing. This is a live trap for the CA audit and for any future measurement of that switch. |

1661.label: MEASURED
1661.text: **ORCH'S PIL TRIAGE LIST CONTAINED A FALSE POSITIVE ON A SHARED READER AND WAS INCOMPLETE IN ORCH'S OWN DIRECTORY.** `ca_radial.py`'s `load_tiff_u16` calls `Image.open` **for the tags only** and reads pixels via `np.memmap(dtype='<u2')`, asserting 16-bit and **validating strip contiguity** rather than assuming a flat layout; it is byte-identical to `tifffile` on five files and is imported by several milestones. Five further scripts in `experiments/ORCH-drift-check/` **were** affected and unlisted, of which **`patchwork_16bit.py` is the worst case in the project**: a script named for 16-bit handling that reads pixels through PIL and then derives full scale as `np.iinfo(a.dtype).max`, giving **255 instead of 65535** on top of already quantised data. Separately, fact 1374's `nearest > catmull-rom` hair-resolution result was re-run under both readers and is **reader-independent**. |

1662.label: MEASURED
1662.text: **ORCH'S `61.0 %` CA HEADLINE IS REAL, MEASURED ON A CLEAN ARM, AND MIS-DESCRIBED.** Unlike the halo failure of fact 1596, the figure comes from a **full-frame, aligned, default-gate, default-resampler, full-stack** render -- the audit checked the argv, and that part is clean. But it is **not a chroma reduction**: it is the fall in edge-localised chroma **excess**, a derived contrast against a baseline five pixels away. The same correction on the same file gives raw edge chroma **-29.4 %**, near-edge **-20.5 %**, and whole-frame **-4.9 %**. **ORCH quoted the largest of five available numbers for one effect, without the qualifier that makes it mean what it means.** |

1663.label: MEASURED
1663.text: **NO AUTHOR ANYWHERE RECOMMENDS ENABLING `STREHL_FIX_CA` BY DEFAULT; TWO RECOMMEND AGAINST, AND SO DOES THE CODE.** A whitespace-collapsed sentence scan of all `docs/**/*.md` (`v4_absence_check.py`) found the recommendation has **no source** -- it originated with ORCH. Against it: a fit on **20 ROIs** where its own author says a shipped correction needs 100; a coefficient that differs **23.6 %** between two scenes through the same glass; an out-of-sample transfer that **split 0.950 / 0.541** against a 0.60 bar; over-correction that **flips the residual's sign** on both stacks checked; and movement of **blue**, a channel it declares it does not touch, by >4 display levels on up to **2.26 %** of pixels by an unidentified mechanism. |

1664.label: ARGUED
1664.text: **THE CORRECTION IS NEVERTHELESS BETTER, AND THE BY-EYE CLAIM SURVIVED AUDIT.** The 5x-crop judgement was ruled a real observation rather than an ORCH paraphrase, independently reproduced. The audit's own recommendation is therefore **keep the default OFF and recommend the flag scoped to the owner's own optical path** -- `STREHL_FIX_CA=a7c2-fe100gm-2xtc-x4cpl`, which is **case-sensitive**, with `1` / `true` / `on` **deliberately rejected** so the software never guesses a lens, and a typo raised as an error rather than a silent no-op. Three standing caveats: fringes get **fainter, not thinner**; the residual is **red-biased**; and it has **never been compared against anything but an arm that does no resampling at all**. |

1665.label: MEASURED
1665.text: **THE PROJECT'S HEADLINE CA NUMBER HAS NEVER BEEN MEASURED IN THE SPACE THE PROJECT SAYS TO MEASURE IN.** The `61.0 %` was taken in `--srgb`, whose own `--help` reads *For looking at, NOT for measuring*, and which M113 measured as **cross-channel contaminated** (chain transfer 1.3073 against 0.9399 / 0.9813 binned-linear). The `lin-*.tif` renders already exist, so the re-measurement is cheap. Ranked second of five things that would change the verdict, behind running the **`anti` arm** (negative-strength vs on), which needs only a strength knob in `optics.rs` and **one render**. |
